project_type: Next.js 16.4.2 app-router (Turbopack, cacheComponents enabled) + Drizzle ORM (postgres-js driver) + Supabase Postgres + Zod v4 + iron-session + Razorpay + Inngest + Resend + react-email + @react-pdf/renderer. React 19.3.0.
language: TypeScript (strict). Email and PDF templates are .tsx React components.
build_system: npm. `next build` (Turbopack) for type-check/build. `npm run test` = `vitest --run`. Drizzle migrations via `npx drizzle-kit generate` (writes SQL to db/migrations/) and `npx drizzle-kit push` (applies to DB). next.config.ts has `cacheComponents: true` and `partialPrefetching: true`. A pre-existing peer-dependency conflict is resolved with `--legacy-peer-deps` (packages are already installed; do NOT reinstall).
test_framework: vitest. Config in vitest.config.ts: globals:true, environment 'node', alias '@' -> workspace root. Existing tests live in services/*.test.ts and lib/validations/*.test.ts. The task explicitly says DO NOT add new tests; only ensure existing tests still pass.
verification_instructions: 1) Run `npm run build` and confirm zero TypeScript/compiler errors and a successful build. 2) Run `npm run test` and confirm all existing tests pass (cart.service.guest.test.ts, lib/validations/checkout.test.ts, lib/validations/cart.test.ts). 3) Re-read each created/modified file and confirm it matches the spec exactly. 4) For the schema change, run `npx drizzle-kit generate` and confirm a new migration SQL adding the 3 boolean columns is created; attempt `npx drizzle-kit push` (DATABASE_URL is in .env.local).
snapshot_or_generated_files: db/migrations/<NNNN>_<name>.sql produced by `npx drizzle-kit generate` (checked in to the repo). tsconfig.tsbuildinfo and .next/ are build artifacts (gitignored). next-env.d.ts is generated by Next.
environment_constraints: 1) `npx drizzle-kit push` can HANG on the Supabase transaction pooler (known issue). The generated SQL is still correct; if push hangs, apply the generated migration SQL via psql or note it for manual application. `npm run build` does NOT depend on push succeeding (build only compiles). 2) ALL notification env vars (RESEND_API_KEY, RESEND_FROM_EMAIL, MSG91_AUTH_KEY, MSG91_SENDER_ID, MSG91_TEMPLATE_ID, WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN, WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID, INNGEST_EVENT_KEY, INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY) are PRESENT in .env.local but currently EMPTY — they must be filled with placeholder test values. .env.example already documents all of them. Do not overwrite existing real values for non-notification vars. 3) Inngest auto-reads INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY and INNGEST_EVENT_KEY from process.env; no need to pass them explicitly to `new Inngest(...)` or `serve(...)`. 4) The Inngest route /api/inngest is reachable through the existing middleware.ts (it only redirects /account and /admin; /api passes through). No middleware/proxy change is required. 5) cacheComponents:true means route handlers are dynamic by default (good for webhooks). 6) Never expose Resend/MSG91/WhatsApp/Inngest keys to the client; all sending happens server-side (Inngest functions, server actions, route handlers).
contribution_requirements: AGENTS.md (workspace) mandates reading node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing Next.js code and notes that in Next.js 16 'middleware' is renamed to 'proxy' (functionality unchanged; the existing middleware.ts still works and does NOT need renaming for this task). Match existing project conventions exactly: 'use server' directive at the top of action files; @/ path alias (tsconfig paths '@/*' -> './*'); ApiResponse wrapper (ok/err) from @/lib/api-response for action/route responses; Zod schemas live in lib/validations/*.ts with inferred types; Drizzle query patterns (db.select/insert/update, db.transaction(async tx => {...})); typed responses; numeric DB columns are strings. Do NOT add new tests. Commit locally on the branch; never push.
key_patterns: Actions (actions/*.ts): top line `"use server"`; import { db } from '@/db', schema from '@/db/schema', getUser/requireAdmin/requireAuth from '@/lib/auth', { ok, err, type ApiResponse } from '@/lib/api-response'; Zod-parse input with .safeParse and return err on failure; return ApiResponse<T>. Route handlers (app/api/.../route.ts): export async function POST(request: NextRequest); use request.json()/request.text(); NextResponse.json(ok(...)/err(...), { status }); wrap in try/catch. Service modules (services/*.ts): plain TS, import { db } and schema, return typed results, no 'use server'. Validations (lib/validations/*.ts): z.object schemas + exported z.infer types. DB (db/index.ts): `export const db = drizzle(client, { schema })`; schema barrel in db/schema/index.ts re-exports everything. Auth (lib/auth.ts): getUser() returns the Supabase auth user (id/email) or null; getUserProfile() returns the profiles row or null; requireAuth() redirects to /login if unauthenticated; requireAdmin() redirects to / if not admin. Numeric order columns (subtotal/total/etc.) are stored as strings; Number() to compute. orders.shippingAddress is a jsonb ShippingAddress (recipientName, phone, addressLine1, addressLine2?, city, state, postalCode).

directory_structure: app/api/{payments/{create-order,verify,webhook},categories,products} route handlers; app/(auth), app/(dashboard) route groups; actions/ (server actions); services/ (business logic); db/schema/ (Drizzle tables/enums), db/migrations/ (generated SQL); lib/{validations,supabase}/; components/{emails,forms,shared,ui}/; config/site.ts; types/. emails/ and components/emails/ currently contain only .gitkeep.

inngest_4.24.0.client: `new Inngest({ id: 'kartiva' })` — auto-reads INNGEST_EVENT_KEY and INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY from process.env.
inngest_4.24.0.route: `import { serve } from 'inngest/next'; export const { GET, POST, PUT } = serve({ client: inngest, functions: [...] });` in app/api/inngest/route.ts. serve options require `client` and `functions`.
inngest_4.24.0.createFunction: INSTALLED 2-arg form: `inngest.createFunction({ id, retries: 3, triggers: [{ event: 'notification/order.confirmed' }] }, async ({ event, step }) => {...})`. CRITICAL: the spec's documented 3-arg form `createFunction({ id, retries }, { event }, handler)` is OUTDATED for v4 and would be a TypeScript error — use the 2-arg form with `triggers` inside the options object. `retries` is 0..20.
inngest_4.24.0.step: `step.run('step-name', async () => {...})` for retry-granular units. `event.data` holds the payload; `event.name` holds the event name.
inngest_4.24.0.send: `await inngest.send({ name: 'notification/order.confirmed', data: { userId, orderId } })` — the installed send takes a single { name, data } payload object (the README's old 2-arg send('name', { data }) is deprecated). Wrap every inngest.send() in try/catch so a notification dispatch failure never breaks the order/payment flow.

schema_decisions.profiles_opt_in_columns: Add to db/schema/profiles.ts: `emailNotifications: boolean('email_notifications').notNull().default(true)`, `smsNotifications: boolean('sms_notifications').notNull().default(true)`, `whatsappNotifications: boolean('whatsapp_notifications').notNull().default(true)`. Import `boolean` from drizzle-orm/pg-core (profiles.ts currently omits it). Defaults of true keep existing rows opted-in. Generate a Drizzle migration; the columns are ADD ... DEFAULT true NOT NULL so existing tests/rows are unaffected.
schema_decisions.notifications_log_usage: db/schema/notifications_log.ts ALREADY has: id, userId (FK set null), channel (enum email/sms/whatsapp/push), recipient, subject, templateId, payload (jsonb), status (enum pending/sent/failed), errorMessage, sentAt, createdAt. There are NO dedicated `eventType` or `providerMessageId` columns — store BOTH inside the `payload` jsonb (e.g. payload: { eventType, providerMessageId, ... }). Do NOT add new columns; use the table as-is. This satisfies 'log each attempt (channel, event type, recipient, status, error, provider message id, timestamps)' without a schema migration on this table.
